items.title: Only half of Telangana cops are trained in new criminal laws, says Home Ministry
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Only half of Telangana’s police officials have been trained in the new criminal laws introduced via the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). According to data released by the Union government, only 27,747 (52.2%) of the total 53,115 police officers have been trained in the new criminal laws that replaced the earlier Indian Penal Code (IPC). The data was released during the ongoing monsoon session by Minister of State for Union Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay in response to a question posed by Rajya Sabha Leader of Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge. While prosecutors, judicial officers and forensic experts in Telangana have been trained completely in the new laws, several police officials remain untrained. Additionally, only 680 out of 1,110 (61%) prison personnel have been trained in BNS. In comparison, other south Indian states have fared better. Out of 56,773 police officers, Andhra Pradesh has trained 54,764 – a 96.36% rate. Karnataka has trained 44,860 police officials out of 45,324 (98.97%), Kerala has trained 48,623 out of 52,808 (92.07%), and Tamil Nadu has trained 93,075 out of 1,00,970 officials (92.18%). items.title: Supreme Court refuses to issue uniform policy against demolition of long-standing properties, asks States to consider
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday declined to entertain a petition seeking a uniform policy across the country for regularisation and demolition of long-standing unauthorised constructions. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana said such issues essentially fall within the policy domain and thus declined the prayer for constitution a court-empowered committee to formulate uniform guidelines on the subject. The Court noted that circumstances vary from State to State and thus different policy frameworks may be needed to deal with facts of each case. "It would be difficult and may not be prudent for this Court to lay down a uniform policy framework to be applied across various States," the Court said. However, the Court said the States and Union Territories may consider the issues raised in the petition filed by Centre for Law and Good Governance for the purpose of formulating or revisiting their existing policies. "We are hopeful that due consideration shall be given to all such issues by the competent authorities," it said. Justice M Nagaprasanna said that criminal investigation cannot be permitted to disable a functioning healthcare institution. items.title: Every case has a hole. Find yours first.
items.summary: There is a particular silence that falls in a courtroom when the bench asks a question nobody on your team had considered. Every litigator in India knows that silence. You have read the brief four times. Your junior has tabbed the compilation. You have gone over the opening in the car, in the lift, in the corridor outside the court. And then, somewhere in the second paragraph of your submission, a judge looks up from the file and asks one short question that goes directly to the weakest part of your case. You recover. You seek a short accommodation, you offer to address it after the break, you find something in the record. But you know what has happened. The case did not fail. You met your own weakness in front of the bench rather than in your chamber. That moment is what we set out to move. Not to remove it, but to move it earlier. Every good lawyer already knows After years spent around courts, legal data, and the people who practise law, one thing has become clear to me. The NCW, on August 10, signed a memorandum of understanding ( MOU ) with the Karnataka government to set up Pre-Marital Communication Centres (PMCCs) at each of the 175 Santwana Kendras run by the state government. The MOU was signed under the NCW’s ‘Tere Mere Sapne’ (Your dreams and mine) initiative. In Kannada, the programme is called ‘Koodi Baalona’, meaning living together. Under the programme, the NCW will provide standardised training modules, train the trainers, and monitor implementation. Training sessions were held across the state in Bengaluru on August 10. Addressing the media, Chairperson of Karnataka State Commission for Women Nagalakshmi Choudhary said that the programme would help young couples discuss issues before their wedding with trained counsellors, aiming to avoid problems in the future. items.title: The other side of the Kanwar Yatra: What women face on the road
items.summary: For devotees of Lord Shiva, the month of Sawan is a time to embark on a journey of faith. Kanwariyas travel from Haridwar carrying Ganga water, often walking for days before returning home to offer it at a nearby Shiva temple on Shivratri. In recent years, more women have joined the Kanwar Yatra, undertaking the journey alongside men. But what is the experience like for them? What challenges do they face on the road, and what keeps them going? We spoke to women kanwariyas to understand their journeys and the difficulties they encounter along the way. Kirti tells us how she is making the long journey with her husband and their seven-month-old baby. Khushboo, meanwhile, speaks about her love for sports and the challenges that come with pursuing it.
